result: The ssDNA drop-in method successfully generated GFP-tagged proteins marking organelles in S2R+ cells. Using PCR-generated ssDNA donors with 100 nt homology arms and Lambda Exonuclease treatment, 19 of 20 targeted genes showed GFP signal by FACS (1-4% frequency), with 12 genes yielding verified clones showing correct subcellular localization and precise insertions.
evaluation: Claims C2-C17, C54, C62, C66, and C68 collectively demonstrate successful implementation of the ssDNA method in S2R+ cells. The data show appropriate controls (PCR verification, sequencing, Western blots, immunostaining), consistent results across multiple genes, and validation against known protein localizations. The ~60% success rate (12/20 genes) is well-documented with supporting figures and tables.

result: The ssDNA drop-in method with attP-3XP3-EGFP-attP cassette (1442 nt) was tested for in vivo fly transgenesis but proved less efficient than standard CRIMIC constructs. Only 4 genes were successfully targeted with ssDNA versus 4 with CRIMIC, with CRIMIC producing more independent lines per gene.
evaluation: Claims C18-C23 and C71 provide direct experimental comparison between ssDNA and CRIMIC methods for the same 10 genes using identical gRNAs. The data clearly show lower efficiency of ssDNA for germline transformation despite success in cell culture. The size limitation (~2 kb) is empirically determined and the comparative results are presented in Figure 3B.

result: Two shortened dsDNA drop-in constructs were developed and tested: attP-SA-3XSTOP-minipolyA-U6gRNA1-attP (715 nt) and attP-SA-T2A-miniGAL4-minipolyA-U6gRNA1-attP (1968 nt). These yielded 65 and 119 independent transgenic lines respectively across 10 genes, with 7/10 genes verified by PCR for both constructs, suggesting >70% precise recombination rate.
evaluation: Claims C24-C35 describe the design rationale and experimental results for shortened constructs. The use of miniGAL4, U6:gRNA1 marker, and minipolyA is well-justified by size constraints and prior literature (C24, C25, C30). The high number of transgenic lines obtained and PCR verification rate support the claimed efficiency, though 3 genes failed due to gRNA target site variations in the injection stock.

result: The mutagenic efficacy of shortened constructs was assessed by Western blot. The attP-SA-3XSTOP-minipolyA-U6gRNA1-attP construct caused ~40% protein reduction, while attP-SA-T2A-miniGAL4-minipolyA-U6gRNA1-attP caused ~80-90% reduction (similar to CRIMIC). MiniGAL4 drove ~60% lower reporter expression than full-length GAL4.
evaluation: Claims C36-C38 present quantitative Western blot data comparing protein levels across constructs, supported by Figure 5A-B. The mechanistic speculation in C73-C75 is appropriately labeled as inference/speculation. The functional limitation of miniGAL4 (C76, C38) is empirically demonstrated, though the statistical analysis details (sample size, replicates) could be more explicit for C36-C37.

result: A drop-in int100-CRIMIC strategy was developed using synthesized vectors ($80) with 100 nt homology arms flanking restriction sites, followed by single-step cloning of full CRIMIC cassettes. This successfully targeted 5/7 genes tested, demonstrating that 100 nt homology arms suffice for large (~5 kb) insertions, with functional validation showing similar expression patterns to conventional CRIMIC.
evaluation: Claims C39-C43, C51, and C82 describe a practical solution to cost and cloning challenges. The experimental data (5/7 genes successfully targeted, PCR verification, expression pattern comparison in Figure 6C and supplement) support the approach. Cost estimates are explicit and the single-step cloning advantage is clearly demonstrated compared to the multi-step CRIMIC protocol.

result: In vivo linearization of donor plasmids by Cas9 cutting at flanking gRNA1 sites improves homologous recombination efficiency. This approach, combined with 100 nt homology arms, enables efficient and precise integration of 1-5 kb cassettes in Drosophila germline.
evaluation: Claims C4-C6, C30, C52, and C83 describe the in vivo linearization strategy. The approach is supported by prior literature in other organisms (C30) and the experimental results across multiple constructs and genes demonstrate improved efficiency. The precision of integration is verified by sequencing (C15, C33) and PCR validation.

result: The drop-in methods are faster, cheaper, and more efficient than conventional CRIMIC. The cloning success rate is nearly 100% versus ~50% for CRIMIC, and overall success rate is 70-80% versus ~50%, with reduced cost (~$100 vs ~$300 per construct) and bench time.
evaluation: Claims C7, C48-C50, and C53 summarize the comparative advantages. These are supported by the accumulated data across all experiments, cost breakdowns (C8, C29, C39, C40, C51), and workflow comparisons (C54, Figure 1B). The success rates are empirically derived from the experimental results presented throughout the manuscript.

result: The U6-gRNA1 dominant marker has significant limitations: it requires additional transgenes for detection and segregates independently from the targeted gene, making stock establishment and maintenance more challenging.
evaluation: Claims C77-C79 identify practical limitations of the U6-gRNA1 marker system. These are clearly stated and supported by Figure 4—figure supplement 1 showing the detection scheme. The limitations are acknowledged as trade-offs for the size reduction benefit, providing balanced assessment of the method.

result: Background on CRIMIC methodology: The conventional CRIMIC method uses dsDNA donors with ~1 kb homology arms to insert ~5 kb cassettes, costs $1,000-2,000 per line, and has ~50% overall success rate. This contrasts with ssDNA methods that typically use 50-100 nt homology arms for small (~200 nt) insertions.
evaluation: Claims C1, C8-C9, and C57-C60 provide context from prior work and established methods. These are appropriately cited (C1, C57-C60) or based on the authors' accumulated experience (C8-C9). The claims establish the baseline against which the new methods are compared.

result: Comparison with homology-independent methods: In vivo linearization without homology arms has been shown in other organisms but is error-prone and non-directional. In Drosophila, Bosch et al. (2019) achieved 4/11 success rate with error-prone insertions, while in vitro linearized DNA is a poor substrate for Drosophila germline transformation.
evaluation: Claims C44-C47 and C80-C81 appropriately cite and summarize prior work on alternative approaches. The citations support the stated limitations of homology-independent methods and provide context for why the authors chose homology-dependent approaches with short arms as a middle ground.

result: Additional methodological context and applications: The SA-GFP-SD tag preserves function in 75% of cases; S2R+ cells used are derivatives with mCherry::Clic; genes with low expression may have insufficient signal-to-noise for clone isolation; prior PCR-based methods achieved ~2% efficiency with drug selection; asymmetric homology arms may improve efficiency; the generated cell lines are useful resources for organelle studies.
evaluation: Claims C55-C56, C61, C63-C65, C67, C69-C70, C72, and C85 provide supporting context, methodological details, and discussion of applications. These are appropriately cited where drawing on prior work (C55-C56, C61, C65, C67, C69-C70) or clearly stated as speculation/inference where appropriate (C64, C72, C85).
